questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have always dreamt of being a journalist, and Universidad Complutense de Madrid was the only partner university with the option to have journalistic subjects. Besides, I really like Madrid and I wanted to try to live here for some time.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The international relations office at the faculty of information has been really helpful. When you arrive in a new country - and at a new university - sometimes it can be difficult to understand how exactly everything works, and there is a lot of information at the same time. The secretaries at the international relations office have been very welcoming and quick to respond.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Before the arrival, I received several emails from the internacional relations office with information about the arrival. The Friday before the semester began there was an information meeting for exchange students at the faculty of information about the matriculation process, but unfortunately I couldn't attend because of my exams at UCPH. There was also an information meeting for all Erasmus students at UCM, which was also very helpful. Apart from that, as mentioned before, the international relations office has been very helpful in all regards.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Even though it can be difficult to find housing in Madrid, in my case it wasn't that bad. I found an apartment through a website called Spotahome together with two study buddies from UCPH who were also going to Madrid. My recommendations would be to start looking well in advance and to rent the apartment or room through Spotahome, since they are all verified.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Since I arrived with two friends from UCPH, it has been working really well to live off campus. For me, it has been a good way to get a break from the university environment. Though, when you live off campus, having a social life within the university requieres that you take initiative, participate in social gatherings, etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I would say that I am overall satisfied with the housing available for students, even though it can be a little expensive compared to other Spanish cities, especially if you don't find your housing well it advance (we paid 600 euros each). I know that Universidad Complutense has student residencies available, but I'm not quite sure if they are available for Erasmus students.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Before arrival, the international relations office sends you a couple of documents that must be filled in and signed upon arrival as a part of the matriculation process. You are responsible for putting together your own schedule, which means that already while you apply for "forhåndsgodkendelse" at UCPH you must check if the subjects overlap. If not, you have to apply for an updated "forhåndsgodkendelse" with new subjects which can delay the process a lot. Once you find out what subjects you are able to attend, you show up at class and get the professor from each subject to sign a document that approves your participation in the subject. Once all that is done, the international relations office can finish the matriculation process.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: As mentioned before, the internacional relations office has been really helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Luckily, I managed to sign up for all the subjects I wanted and that appeared in my "forhåndsgodkendelse", because I checked the schedule of each subject while I applied for the "forhåndsgodkendelse".

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The most important thing is to read carefully all the emails and documents that you receive, fill in the documents in time and, as I mentioned before, take a look at the schedule of each subject while you apply for your "forhåndsgodkendelse".

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level has varied a lot from course to course, but generally it has been lower than at UCPH. Though, the work load has been quite high, since there are a lot of written assignments and presentations throughout the semester and because you have 5 different subjects at the same time.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching in Spain reminds me a bit of high school, because of all the (mandatory) written assignments and presentations throughout the semester and because they register attendance in class. There has been a lot of dialogue and interaction in class, at least in my subjects, which surprised me positively, but still there are a lot of memorizing. The lack of flexibility and perhaps self-determination has been a bit frustrating sometimes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: My favorite subject has been "pragmática y discurso en el periodismo" with the professor Raquel Taranilla García. It has been very "practical" because we got to write and analyse different journalistic texts from the news media, and I had the opportunity to make usage of cultural and linguistic knowledge. Raquel has been very friendly, helpful and willing to consider our situation as exchange students. She is definitely one of the best professors I have ever had.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Medicin in connection with illness.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Especially public transportation has been way cheaper than I expected. As a student, you can use all public transportation in Madrid with a cost of 8 euros per month. Though, food in the supermarket has been more expensive than I expected (it is almost as expensive as in Denmark).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Universidad Complutense offers a lot of different activities. There are a lot of sports facilities and teams, and the university collaborates with a variety of cultural institutions.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I had a fitness membership through the university, where I could access fitness facilities and take different classes such as pilates and yoga. For me it was nice not having a fixed schedule as I would have had if I was a part of a football team or the like, because there are quiete a lot of written assignments, as I mentioned before.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: First of all, I would recommend exploring different neighborhoods in Madrid. Also, there are several nice places outside Madrid such as Toledo, Segovia and Alcalá de Henares. Madrid is very well-connected, and it's easy to take high-speed trains to other parts of Spain.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: For me, it has been quite easy, since I already spoke Spanish when I arrived. Generally, the locals are very welcoming, open-minded and easy to talk to. They would often help you if you are in doubt of anything, invite you to social gatherings, etc.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: One of the things that made it easier for me to socialize with local students has been all the group work at the university. This allowed me to get to know the other students better. Apart from that, it is always a good idea to participate in cultural and athletic activities at the university.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Even though this is not only a cultural matter, I would say the age gap between me and the local students. Most Spanish students go directly from high school to university, which means they are really young and don't have a lot of experience.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I appreciated the mentality of the Spanish people. They are very social, talkative and open-minded, and they don't necessarily take things so seriously.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be aware that the style of teaching is different compared with that of UCPH, be open-minded and try to interact as much as possible with the local students.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No, nothing that I havn't mentioned already.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To try to live in a new country and all the amazing people I met.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting use to a different style of teaching.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
